summary: Verified both requested fixes and regressions against the public URL. Landing copy, booking, admin dashboard, lead APIs, bcrypt/cookies, and data persistence pass. Public CORS and brute-force behavior still fail despite working correctly when the backend is addressed directly: the edge injects wildcard CORS, and alternating ingress proxy addresses split the per-IP login counter.

critical.issue: Through the required public URL, both https://evil.example and the legitimate frontend origin receive Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *. The arbitrary origin must receive no ACAO header. Direct backend diagnostics show the FastAPI allowlist is correct, so the public Cloudflare/Google ingress is intercepting preflight and injecting/overriding wildcard CORS headers.

Six failed public login attempts for a unique throwaway email returned 401 six times instead of 401 x5 then 429. Backend access logs show requests alternate between ingress source addresses 10.219.1.6 and 10.219.1.32; request.client.host therefore creates separate counters for one caller. A successful public login can likewise leave the counter associated with the other proxy address uncleared. Direct-backend attempts correctly return 429 on attempt six.

action_items: Configure the public ingress/gateway so it does not inject Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * and allows the backend explicit-origin CORS policy to control preflight and actual responses.

Make login throttling identify the real client consistently behind trusted proxies (configure trusted forwarded headers/proxy CIDRs), or use a stable account-based key; then verify the sixth public attempt returns 429 and successful login clears all applicable counters.
Retest both security fixes through REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL rather than localhost.
critical_code_review_comments: login() keys lockout state with request.client.host, which is an ingress proxy address in this deployment and changes across requests. This makes the lockout bypassable and prevents reliable counter clearing.

server.py's CORSMiddleware allowlist is correct in direct-backend diagnostics, but the public edge handles OPTIONS itself and adds wildcard CORS to actual responses, so application-only CORS configuration does not enforce the public security boundary.

/app/auth_testing.md was absent; credentials were read from /app/memory/test_credentials.md as required. Stored admin hash was verified as $2b$, login set two HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite=None cookies, and seed_admin source updates an existing hash when ADMIN_PASSWORD changes.

success_rate.frontend: 100% of requested desktop flows plus mobile navigation/overflow checks

seed_data_creation: Created one TEST_QA_ backend lead and one TEST_QA_UI_ITER2 booking lead; all TEST_QA_ leads and all login_attempts records were removed after testing (verified zero remaining).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Keep using the public URL. CORS and brute-force both pass against 127.0.0.1:8001 but fail externally. Backend logs identify alternating ingress peers 10.219.1.6/10.219.1.32. All landing, booking, admin, API validation/status/serialization regressions passed. Use a throwaway lockout email and clear login_attempts after retest.
rca_of_the_issue: Public CORS failure is introduced at the Cloudflare/Google ingress: public OPTIONS returns 204 wildcard headers without reaching FastAPI, and wildcard headers are also appended to actual responses. Brute-force failure is caused by using request.client.host behind a load-balanced reverse proxy; one attacker is partitioned into multiple ip:email MongoDB records as proxy source addresses alternate. Configure trusted proxy forwarding or use a stable identifier, and fix edge CORS behavior.
